result.markdown:
The best HR software for a small company depends on whether you need employee management, payroll, leave tracking, recruitment, performance reviews or all of these.

**My top recommendation for a small Australian business would be to look at Employment Hero first**, particularly if you want an HR platform that can grow with your company.

There are several good alternatives, though, and the best choice depends on your team's size and how much HR administration you want to automate.

## Best HR software for small businesses

My shortlist for 2026

(Best overall for Australia)

## Quick comparison

| Software | Main strength | My verdict |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Employment Hero | Australian HR and payroll | Best starting point |
| BambooHR | Core HR management | Excellent |
| Rippling | Automation and IT | Best for tech businesses |
| HiBob | Engagement and culture | Best for growing teams |
| Zoho People | Affordability | Best for tight budgets |


One important consideration: US-focused platforms such as Gusto aren't necessarily suitable for Australian payroll and employment requirements. Make sure your chosen platform supports Australian awards, leave entitlements, superannuation, STP reporting and Fair Work obligations.

Recent comparisons also rate BambooHR highly for core HR and Rippling for automation. [technologyadvice.com](https://technologyadvice.com/blog/human-resources/best-hr-software-for-small-business/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.techradar.com](https://www.techradar.com/best/best-hr-software?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[zapier.com](https://zapier.com/blog/best-hr-software-for-small-businesses/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## What I'd choose

- **5–15 employees\:** Employment Hero or Zoho People.
- **15–50 employees\:** Employment Hero or BambooHR.
- **50–100 employees\:** Employment Hero, Rippling or HiBob.

These are starting recommendations rather than hard employee-count limits.

## Let me narrow it down for your company

I'd like to recommend the best system rather than just the most popular one.

**How many employees does your company have?**

And is your biggest priority having\:

- Employee records, contracts and onboarding
- Leave requests and approvals
- Timesheets and rostering
- Payroll and superannuation
- Performance reviews and staff management
- Everything in one integrated HR system

If you tell me your approximate employee numbers and priorities, I can narrow this down to the **best three options for an Australian small business**, including pricing, pros and cons, and which one I'd actually buy.

search_results.description: TechRadar’s 2026 guide evaluates leading HR software for payroll, compliance, recruitment, onboarding, benefits, performance management, and employee administration. Gusto is named best overall for its full-service payroll, time tracking, benefits administration, compliance support, and HR guidance. Employment Hero is recommended for small and medium-sized businesses because of its customizable workflows, automation, AI assistant, and broad feature set, though advanced functions and add-ons can increase costs. Rippling is best for versatility, particularly for distributed teams, offering remote device management, tax registration, scalable services, and per-employee billing. Other recommendations include Remote Payroll for international enterprises, BambooHR as an all-in-one system, Zoho People for integrations, Breathe HR for simple employee management, Deel for powerful global HR capabilities, PeopleHR for mobile access, Paylocity for mid-sized businesses, Staffology Payroll for complex enterprise payroll, Workable for recruitment, and BrightHR for extensive workforce-management features. The guide advises selecting software according to company size and specific workflow needs, and explains that testing considered usability, features, security, support, pricing, and user feedback.
